listing.description: Welcome to 33 Eastwood Ct, a beautifully updated sanctuary tucked into a quiet cul de sac in the Montclair Hills. Thoughtfully refreshed throughout, this home features new siding, energy-efficient windows, a tankless water heater, Carrier furnace and new appliances. The main entry opens to bright, open living spaces with gleaming hardwood floors and large windows framing peaceful treetop views. A majestic redwood just outside creates a sense of privacy and a beautiful connection to nature. The newly remodeled kitchen offers a functional layout and access to a cozy, private patio ideal for morning coffee, outdoor dining, or relaxed entertaining. All bedrooms are conveniently situated together upstairs. The spacious primary suite enjoys lovely treetop views, an en-suite bathroom, and generous closet space. Another bedroom features sliding-door access to its own peaceful patio, while laundry on this level makes everyday living easy. With a spacious attached two car garage, this move-in ready home blends modern comfort with a tranquil woodland setting, just minutes from the shops and dining of Montclair Village. Welcome Home!

view.note: Treetop/canyon canopy over neighbor rooftops from the window wall (p_08, p_12, p_25); bay/SF visible only at drone altitude (p_48), not from living level; power lines intrude into the view corridor (p_06, p_07).

natural_light.note: Vaulted white living room with 4-pane window wall + double sliders is genuinely bright (p_09, p_12, p_15); but sink window faces dense magnolia (p_22), bedrooms are moderate (p_24, p_31), and the 3rd bedroom leans on its patio door for light (p_34); tall redwoods filter sun all day.

character.note: 1970 shed-roof tri-level with painted post-and-beam + T&G vaulted ceilings and open rafter tails (p_10, p_11, p_16) — MCM-lite bones; full white paint-out and standard flip finishes mute some of it; dated white spindle railing retained (p_14).

kitchen.note: Genuinely new mid-range remodel: rift-oak flat fronts, waterfall quartz peninsula, gas slide-in range, SS French-door fridge, glass display uppers, buffet wall (p_16, p_18, p_19, p_21, p_23) — but no visible hood and no tile backsplash, just painted drywall (p_20, p_22).

privacy.note: Quiet cul-de-sac + magnolia/redwood green screens help (p_16, p_43); but hillside neighbors sit ~15–40 ft away (p_07, p_40), and a neighbor's elevated deck overlooks the rear patio (p_38, p_40).

layout_flow.note: Tri-level per floorplan (p_51): living+deck at entry level, kitchen/dining a half-flight up, 3 bedrooms + laundry on top — good vertical separation and direct deck access from living (p_13); stairs everywhere, no single-level living.

primary_suite.note: Corner primary 14'x17' with two treetop windows (p_29, p_31), ensuite shower bath (p_33), and its own 9'x11' patio per floorplan (p_51); storage is double reach-ins, not the 'generous' walk-in marketing implies (p_31).

outdoor_space.note: 8'x24' view deck off living (p_06, p_49) + walled 16'x14' rear patio (p_37) + primary patio — three usable pads; but deck boards are weathered, the rear patio is shaded/overlooked (p_38, p_39), and the rest of the lot is steep slope (p_41, p_44).

condition.note: New siding/windows/kitchen/baths verified in photos (p_02, p_16-p_22, p_27, p_33); tankless WH / Carrier furnace claimed, not visible; flat/low-slope roof shows aging granular surface + many penetrations (p_43, p_46); mossy block retaining walls and weathered deck framing (p_41, p_49).

lot_usability.note: 0.14 AC that's mostly steep dry-grass slope rising behind the house (p_44, p_45); usable area is the driveway, deck, and two small patios; rear walkway is narrow with aging retaining walls (p_41, p_42).

verdict: A refreshed 1970 tri-level treehouse in Montclair's Shepherd Canyon that trades big views for canopy immersion: you get a bright vaulted post-and-beam living room, three real upstairs bedrooms, a genuinely new kitchen, and two-and-a-half outdoor pads for $639/sf — and in exchange you underwrite Very High fire-zone insurance risk, overhead power lines, an aging flat roof, a post-supported deck, and a steep lot you can barely use. It is a turnkey charmer for a buyer who wants the redwood-wrapped hills under $1M and will do the fire/roof/retaining-wall inspections, not a view property and not a low-risk one.
flags: 🔥 Very High FHSZ (presumptive) — 94611 sits in the 1991 Oakland firestorm footprint: bindable insurance must be quoted before any offer; dense canopy overhanging the roof + dry grass slope behind the house (p_44, p_45, p_46)
⚡ Multiple overhead power lines cross the front of the house and the deck view corridor (p_03, p_04, p_07, p_43)
🏚️ Flat/low-slope roof with an aged-looking granulated surface and many penetrations (p_43, p_45, p_46) — roof age/certification is a must-ask

🪵 Elevated front deck on tall wood posts over the garage (p_02, p_43, p_49) and mossy, visibly aged block retaining walls along the rear walkway (p_41, p_42) — structural + retaining inspection warranted
🌲 Large redwood within ~10 ft of the deck/structure and tree limbs overhanging the low-slope roof (p_43, p_47, p_50) — defensible-space work needed
🍳 Gas range on the peninsula with no visible hood or tile backsplash (p_19, p_20, p_22) — ventilation short-cut from the remodel
👁️ Rear patio is directly overlooked by the uphill neighbor's elevated deck (p_38, p_40) — 'private patio' is only half true
positives: Bright vaulted post-and-beam living room with a true window wall and double sliders to an 8x24 view deck (p_09, p_11, p_13, p_15)
Legitimate 3-bed/2-bath top floor per the measured floorplan — primary 14x17 w/ ensuite + private patio, no 'office fudge' (p_51)
Genuinely new kitchen and both baths; new siding and energy-efficient windows visible in photos (p_16-p_22, p_27, p_33, p_02)
Quiet cul-de-sac at ~1,090 ft elevation in Shepherd Canyon/Montclair; attached 2-car garage; minutes to Montclair Village (p_47, p_51)
Treetop views from living room and both front bedrooms are real, not drone-manufactured (p_08, p_12, p_25, p_32)
orientationInference: View side (living room window wall + deck) faces roughly W/WNW down the Shepherd Canyon draw — drone shot (p_48) aligns the Bay/SF skyline over the street side, and the canyon drains toward the flats; the rear patios get eastern morning light while the front gets filtered afternoon sun through redwoods. Inference from drone horizon + canyon topography, not measured.

crosschecks.result: Mostly verified: 'treetop views' (p_08, p_12, p_25), new kitchen (p_16–p_22), new siding/windows (p_02, p_20), 'majestic redwood' (p_02, p_50). Overstated: 'generous closet space' = double reach-ins (p_31); rear 'private patio' is overlooked by the uphill neighbor's deck (p_38, p_40); 'Valley Views' amenity = canopy only — the Bay/SF vista exists only from drone altitude (p_48). Unverifiable from photos: tankless water heater, Carrier furnace, new appliances claims.

FLAGGED: Census geocoder pin (37.8352807, -122.1865329) sits ~169 ft NW of the Compass MLS pin (37.8350074, -122.1860619) — just over the 150 ft threshold; both are on the same short cul-de-sac, so this is parcel-pin noise, not a mislocated listing.
1,087 ft at geocoder pin, 1,125 ft at page pin (USGS EPQS) — true Oakland hills; Shepherd Canyon / Montclair (MLS neighborhood MONTCLAIR); steep terrain confirmed by drone (p_44, p_45).

Drone p_48 aligns the Bay/SF skyline over the street side; canyon drops toward the flats — view side (living wall + deck) faces roughly W/WNW down-canyon (inference); rear patios face the uphill slope with eastern morning light. No dusk shots to corroborate.

Very High FHSZ (presumptive) for 94611 inside the 1991 Oakland firestorm footprint — insurance availability flagged: quote before offer; photos show dense canopy overhanging the roof, dry grass slope, wood deck + wood T1-11 siding (p_44–p_46).
'Minutes from Montclair Village' plausible from the map (Shepherd Canyon corridor, ~1–1.5 mi); drone shots are of the actual neighborhood canopy, no borrowed scenery; cul-de-sac confirmed (p_47).

Real 3BR/2BA — measured floorplan (p_51) shows primary 14x17 + bedroom 11x13 + bedroom 10x16 + 2 full baths + laundry 7x10 all on level 4; no office fudge; JSON-LD numberOfRooms '3' matches bedrooms, INITIAL_DATA legalRoomCount 5 counts total rooms — counting convention, not a conflict.
